children: India has moved well beyond its “emerging economy” tag and is now actively shaping global economic institutions, Anuradha Thakur, Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, said at the 13th SBI Banking and Economics Conclave 2026 in Mumbai on Thursday.

Thakur pointed to India’s GDP growth from $2.5 trillion to $4.3 trillion, an inflation-adjusted rise of 77 per cent, the highest among the world’s 20 largest economies over the same period, as the foundation for a larger global role. The World Bank has credited India with reducing the share of its population living in poverty from 57.7 per cent to 16.1 per cent, and extreme poverty from 27.1 per cent to 2.6 per cent.

On trade, Thakur said India has signed nine free trade agreements, spanning 38 countries since 2021. The trade deal with the European Union, concluded in January 2026, will extend preferential access to over 99 per cent of Indian exports and eliminate tariffs of up to 110 per cent on nearly $33 billion worth of labour-intensive goods, including textiles, leather, marine products, and gems.

India’s banking sector is also gaining ground internationally, with SBI and HDFC now ranked among the top 100 banks globally by asset size. Thakur described India’s equity and derivative markets as “ahead of some of the leading economies of the world.”

On food security, India produced 357.73 million tonnes of food grain in 2024-25, about 106 million tonnes more than a decade earlier. In February 2026, the Food Corporation of India signed a five-year MoU with the UN World Food Programme to supply 200,000  tonnes of fortified rice to crisis zones.

Thakur flagged India’s growing role in setting global agendas, noting that India remains a near-permanent invitee to G7 summits despite not being a member, and that an Indian civil servant holds the vice-presidency of the Financial Action Task Force. The BRICS New Delhi Declaration 2026, she said, called for reforms to Bretton Woods institutions to better reflect the weight of emerging and developing economies.

She cautioned, however, that the journey was not complete. it is built when institutions, markets, financial systems, and the nation become sufficiently trusted that others choose to rely upon them,” she said, adding that domestic household savings remained an underutilised channel for deepening the financial system.

title: India has outgrown ‘Emerging Economy’ tag, eyes bigger role in global order: DEA Secretary
